samples_judged.question_text:
Look at the class schedule:
• Math: 8:00 a.m. – 9:00 a.m.
• English: 9:00 a.m. – 9:45 a.m.
How many minutes long is the English class?
A 2-day gardening project starts on Monday. On what day of the week does it end?
A class started at 9:15 a.m. and ended at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes did it last?
A class started at 4:45 p.m. and lasted 5 minutes. What time did it end?

Look at the bus timetable:
• Bus 1: Departs 7:00 a.m., Arrives 8:00 a.m.
• Bus 2: Departs 8:15 a.m., Arrives 9:15 a.m.
According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 2?
The community sports festival ended at 10:00 a.m. after running for 4 hours. What time did it start?
A soccer practice started at 8:30 a.m. and lasted 40 minutes. What time did it end?

Look at the bus timetable:
• Bus 1: Departs 7:00 a.m., Arrives 8:00 a.m.
• Bus 2: Departs 8:15 a.m., Arrives 8:50 a.m.
According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 1?
The community sports festival started at 8:00 a.m. and lasted for 2 hours. What time did it end?
A class started at 7:00 a.m. and lasted 25 minutes. What time did it end?

verdicts.reasoning: The samples are situated word problems that need a computation, not clock-reading: seed 91 gives a soccer practice starting 8:30 a.m. lasting 40 minutes, and seed 78 works backwards from a festival that ended at 10:00 a.m. after 4 hours to find its 6:00 a.m. start.

Both directions of elapsed-time reasoning appear — duration from two clock times (seed 42: 9:15 to 9:35 gives 20 minutes) and end time from a start plus a duration (seed 57: 4:45 p.m. plus 5 minutes; seed 91: 8:30 a.m. plus 40 minutes; seed 118: 8:00 a.m. plus 2 hours).

The 60-minutes-per-hour relation is what the answer turns on in seed 64 and seed 103, where a whole-hour gap (8:15 to 9:15; 7:00 to 8:00) must be reported as 60 minutes, and seed 91 crosses the hour boundary (8:30 + 40 min = 9:10), which cannot be done without it.

No sample ever relates hours to a day. Seeds 78 and 118 use hour-length durations (4 hours, 2 hours) inside a single morning, and every time in the set is a.m. or p.m. within one day, so the 24-hours-in-a-day fact is never needed or shown.
verdicts.action_taken: Filed as a §6F CONTRADICTED finding, unedited. No sample relates hours to a day or exercises the 24-hours-in-a-day conversion/fact; stems only manipulate within-day durations. Sampler/variant gap; carried to Next tick should:.

verdicts.reasoning: Seed 23 is the one sample working in units of days and named weekdays — a 2-day project beginning Monday, with Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday/Friday as options — so ordering the days of the week is the reasoning required, though no sample ever wraps past Sunday.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Seed 23 is ambiguous: keyed Tuesday counts the days inclusively (Monday is day 1), but reading '2 days' as an added interval gives Wednesday, which is offered as a distractor. The stem should say whether the start day counts.

verdicts.reasoning: Three samples present an actual tabulated schedule the pupil must read a row from — seed 64 and seed 103 show a two-row bus timetable with departure and arrival times and ask about a named bus, and seed 11 shows a class schedule with Math and English periods.
